title: [Chapitre] II. Réalisations topologiques des réseaux : notes manuscrites (06/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from p.14): X is a space, A ⊂ X is closed, U = X∖A, and i: U → X is the inclusion. Comp(Z) = Hom_cont(Z,{0,1}) = Γ(Z, F_2) is the Boolean ring of clopen subsets of Z. The 'rives' (banks) of A in X are Riv(A,X) = colim over neighbourhoods V ⊃ A of Comp(V∖A). This is the Boolean ring of germs along A of clopen pieces of the complement. Equivalently, Riv(A,X) = colim_V Γ(V, i_*F_2). On p.14 Grothendieck also forms Ã = Spec(i_*F_2 |A), the relative Stone spectrum over A of the sheaf of Boolean rings i_*F_2 restricted to A. This plays the role of the 'normal boundary', or space of local sides, of A. He notes Comp(Ã) ≃ Γ(A, i_*F_2 |A).

This page:
(1) There is a canonical map (*) Riv(A,X) → Comp(Ã) = Γ(A, i_*F_2|A). It is always injective and is bijective if X is paracompact. This is the standard comparison colim_{V⊃A} F(V) → Γ(A, F|A), applied to F = i_*F_2. Hence, for X paracompact, choosing a rive amounts to choosing a clopen part ('composante') of Ã.
(2) NB: Riv(A,X) is an idempotent F_2-algebra with unit (ρ² = ρ for all ρ), i.e. a Boolean ring. The map (*) is a homomorphism of unital algebras.
(3) Margin: this algebra is zero iff A is open (hence clopen). If A is open, V = A is a neighbourhood and Comp(∅) = 0. Conversely, 1 = 0 forces V∖A = ∅ for some neighbourhood V, so A is open.
(4) A 'bivière' (two-bank datum) of A in X is an unordered pair {ρ, ρ'} in Riv(A) with ρ + ρ' = 1. That is, a splitting of X∖A near A into two complementary germs. If A is not open, then 1 ≠ 0, which forces ρ ≠ ρ'. The bivière is trivial if {ρ,ρ'} = {0,1}. A disconnects X locally iff a nontrivial bivière exists.
(5) In the paracompact case, a bivière is equivalently a decomposition Ã = Ã_1 ⊔ Ã_2 into two clopen pieces.

Purpose: on p.16 this pair is used to define a 'maille' (mesh) structure with node A, and the cutting space Dec_β(A,X). That space is obtained by gluing the two sides Ã_1, Ã_2 back onto A, which doubles A into A×β for the two-element set β. All of this is preparatory to the topological realization of 'réseaux' (graphs/maps embedded in surfaces), where one cuts a surface along a curve.
errors: No mathematical error. Injectivity of colim_{V⊃A} F(V) → Γ(A, F|A) holds for any closed A: a section vanishing at all germs along A vanishes on an open set containing A. Surjectivity holds when X is paracompact (Godement), as stated.

Implicit step: the identification Comp(Ã) = Γ(A, i_*F_2|A) needs Ã to be the relative Stone spectrum (étale-type space over A whose fibres are the Stone spaces of the stalks), so that clopen sets correspond to global sections of the Boolean-ring sheaf. Grothendieck asserts this without proof on p.14. It is true, but it deserves a check that the topology on Ã is the right one (fibrewise compact, proper over A).
The parenthetical 'ρ ≠ ρ'' requires A not open (Riv ≠ 0), not merely A non-empty. The manuscript says 'ouvert', and the marginal NB confirms this.

ideas.what: Boolean ring of germs along A of clopen subsets of the complement ('rives'), and its sheaf-theoretic expression as colimit of sections of i_*F_2
ideas.modern_name: Germs of local components of X∖A at A; relative Freudenthal-type 'ends' of the complement near A
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ends: Freudenthal (1931); local separation and unicoherence: classical continuum theory (Kuratowski, Wilder)

ideas.what: Ã = Spec(i_*F_2|A) as a 'space of sides' of A, analogous to a normalization separating the local branches of the complement
ideas.modern_name: Relative Stone spectrum of a sheaf of Boolean algebras; topological analogue of normalization / separation of branches; normal sphere bundle in the tubular case
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stone duality (Stone 1936); the sheaf-theoretic relative version is folklore

ideas.what: Comparison colim_{V⊃A} F(V) → Γ(A, F|A): injective in general, bijective for X paracompact
ideas.modern_name: Tautness of closed subspaces of paracompact spaces
ideas.where_published: Used in Tôhoku (1957) context and SGA 4 style arguments; standard

ideas.what: 'Bivière': a complementary pair of rives (equivalently a decomposition Ã = Ã_1 ⊔ Ã_2); definition of A locally disconnecting X; preparation for cutting X along A (Dec_β(A,X))
ideas.modern_name: Two-sidedness / local separation of a codimension-one subspace; cutting a surface along a curve
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Riemann cuts; cut-and-paste topology of surfaces)

missed.claim: An intrinsic, sheaf-theoretic and tubular-neighbourhood-free formalism for 'cutting a space along a closed subset'. A Boolean ring of rives, a relative Stone space Ã of sides, and two-sided splittings are used to construct Dec_β(A,X). This framework, apparently designed to topologically realize 'réseaux' (cartes / dessins) in the 1986 notes, does not appear in the published literature on maps or dessins. The ingredients themselves are classical, so this matters for the record of Grothendieck's 1986 approach rather than as a new theorem.
missed.quote: Une bivière de A en X est une paire {ρ,ρ'} d'éléments de Riv(A), telles que ρ+ρ'=1 ... On dit que A disconnecte X loc^t si ∃ bivière non triviale.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This approach gives a general-topological cut-and-paste formalism (no manifold or tubular hypotheses) that could serve tame-topology or o-minimal treatments of maps on surfaces. It also documents how Grothendieck intended to pass from combinatorial maps to topological surfaces.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but routine foundational material: Boolean rings of germs, the paracompact comparison, and a definition of local disconnection. The idiosyncratic sheaf/Stone-spectrum treatment of cutting is characteristic and unpublished, but it contains no result a specialist would find new or surprising.
transcription_corrections: 'si X ponctuel[?]' should read 'si X paracompact' (consistent with NB 2 on p.14). The map is an injection, and a bijection if X is paracompact.
'choisir une rivière' should read 'choisir une rive' (Riv = Rives).
'L'ens des rivières de A en X connexes[?]' should read 'L'ens des rives de A en X'. The word 'composantes de' is struck and replaced by 'rives de A en X'.
'l'élément[?] principal est une loi[?] d'alg. unitaires' is better read as 'l'application (*) est un homom. d'alg. unitaires'.
'(E²=E ∀E∈Riv)': this is the idempotence condition ρ²=ρ for all ρ in Riv.
'si A n'est pas vide[?]' should read 'si A n'est pas ouvert'.
The parenthesis should read roughly '(c'est-à-dire une "décomposition en 2 composantes de X−A au voisinage de A")', not '...de A ... au voisinage de X−A dans Ā'.
Margin: 'NB Cette algèbre Riv est nulle ssi A est ouvert' ('ssi' rather than 'si'). The trailing words are illegible.
'[-Soit dire-] Une bivière, de façon[?]' probably reads: (struck: 'Si X paracompact') 'Une bivière équivaut à / de façon équivalente une paire {Ã_1,Ã_2} telle que Ã = Ã_1 ⊔ Ã_2'.
The term transcribed 'bivière' might be 'birive' (bi-rive), in line with the 'rive' terminology. The reading is uncertain.
